variants.title: SOFT TISSUE ULTRASOUND — VOLAR LEFT FOREARM (NORMAL STUDY)

blocks.x: CLINICAL INDICATION:
Palpable area of concern on the volar left forearm; rule out soft tissue lump.
TECHNIQUE:

Targeted high-frequency linear (12–18 MHz) grayscale and color/power Doppler ultrasound was performed over the region of clinical concern on the volar left forearm, using a standoff gel pad and comparison to the adjacent/contralateral normal soft tissues.
FINDINGS:
Targeted Area / Lesion Evaluation:

Location & Anatomical Layer: High-frequency evaluation over the palpable area of concern on the volar left forearm demonstrates normal cutaneous, subcutaneous adipose, and underlying muscular layers. No discrete solid mass, cystic lesion, fluid collection, or foreign body is identified.
Dimensions & Shape: Not applicable (no discrete lesion identified).
Echotexture & Acoustic Features: Normal echotexture of the cutaneous, subcutaneous, and muscular layers, with no abnormal posterior acoustic enhancement or shadowing.
Color / Power Doppler Vascularity: Normal background soft tissue vascularity with no focal hyperemia.
Relationship to Adjacent Structures: The underlying investing fascia, flexor tendons, and adjacent radial/ulnar neurovascular bundles appear intact and unremarkable.
Surrounding Soft Tissues & Regional Nodes:
No subcutaneous edema ("cobblestoning") or regional lymphadenopathy.
IMPRESSION:
No focal soft tissue mass, fluid collection, or sonographic abnormality at the site of clinical concern on the volar left forearm.

bank_title: SUPERFICIAL SOFT TISSUE ULTRASOUND — PHRASES BANK

bank.title: PART 1: COMMON SUPERFICIAL PATHOLOGIES & HOW RADIOLOGISTS PHRASE THEIR "SIGNATURE"

subs.title: Lipoma
items: Well-circumscribed, encapsulated, oval subcutaneous mass oriented parallel to skin, iso- to hyperechoic with fine linear echogenic striations and absent Doppler flow.

subs.title: Epidermal Inclusion Cyst (Sebaceous Cyst)
items: Well-defined round/oval hypoechoic dermal/subcutaneous lesion with posterior acoustic enhancement, internal echogenic keratin debris ("pseudotestis" appearance), and a thin superficial punctum tract extending to the epidermis.

subs.title: Abscess vs. Cellulitis
items: Cellulitis: Diffuse subcutaneous thickening, increased echogenicity, and fluid tracking between fat lobules ("cobblestone" appearance) with hyperemia, without a drainable fluid collection.

Abscess: Irregular, compressible/fluctuant hypoechoic-to-anechoic fluid collection with swirling echogenic debris on probe compression, posterior enhancement, and a hyperemic peripheral rim (avascular center).

subs.title: Ganglion Cyst
items: Well-defined anechoic or mildly complex multilocular cystic lesion adjacent to a joint capsule or tendon sheath, demonstrating a narrow communicating neck extending toward the joint/tendon, posterior acoustic enhancement, and no internal flow.

subs.title: Foreign Body
items: Linear or angular hyperechoic focus within the subcutaneous tissue casting clean posterior acoustic shadowing (wood/glass/thorn) or comet-tail / reverberation artifact (metal/glass), surrounded by a hypoechoic inflammatory halo.

subs.title: Suspicious / Indeterminate Mass
items: Deep/subfascial location, size greater than 5 cm, irregular/lobulated margins, heterogeneous echotexture, or disorganized internal Doppler vascularity → Radiologist explicitly recommends contrast-enhanced MRI prior to biopsy or excision.

subs.title: Lipoma (Classic Subcutaneous)
items: Within the subcutaneous adipose layer approximately [X.X] mm deep to the skin, there is a well-circumscribed, encapsulated, oval mass oriented parallel to the skin surface measuring [X.X] x [X.X] x [X.X] cm. The lesion is isoechoic to mildly hyperechoic relative to surrounding fat with characteristic thin, linear echogenic striations, mild compressibility, and no internal Doppler flow, consistent with a benign lipoma.

subs.title: Angiolipoma (Painful / Echogenic Variant)
items: Within the subcutaneous fat at the site of focal tenderness, there is a well-circumscribed, homogeneously hyperechoic oval nodule measuring [X.X] x [X.X] cm demonstrating mild internal color Doppler vascularity, typical of a benign angiolipoma.

subs.title: Epidermal Inclusion Cyst (Uncomplicated)
items: Centered within the dermal/superficial subcutaneous layer, there is a well-defined round/oval hypoechoic lesion measuring [X.X] x [X.X] x [X.X] cm with posterior acoustic enhancement, internal echogenic keratin debris ("pseudotestis" appearance), and a thin superficial punctum tract extending to the epidermis. No internal Doppler flow is seen, diagnostic of an epidermal inclusion cyst.

subs.title: Ruptured / Inflamed Epidermal Cyst
items: Irregular, lobulated hypoechoic dermal/subcutaneous lesion measuring [X.X] x [X.X] cm with focal posterior wall disruption, surrounding echogenic inflammatory fat stranding, and marked peripheral hyperemia (avascular center), consistent with a ruptured/inflamed epidermal inclusion cyst.

subs.title: Pilomatricoma (Calcifying Epithelioma)
items: Superficial dermal/subcutaneous well-defined hypoechoic nodule measuring [X.X] x [X.X] cm containing dense internal echogenic calcifications casting strong posterior acoustic shadowing and a thin hypoechoic peripheral rim, characteristic of a pilomatricoma.

subs.title: Uncomplicated Cellulitis (No Drainable Abscess)
items: Diffuse thickening and increased echogenicity of the subcutaneous fat with interstitial anechoic fluid tracking between fat lobules ("cobblestone" appearance) and diffuse hyperemia on color Doppler. No focal fluid collection or drainable abscess is identified.

subs.title: Subcutaneous Abscess
items: Irregular, fluctuant hypoechoic-to-anechoic fluid collection in the subcutaneous tissue measuring [X.X] x [X.X] x [X.X] cm, demonstrating swirling internal echogenic debris on probe compression, posterior acoustic enhancement, and marked peripheral rim hyperemia with an avascular center, consistent with an abscess.

subs.title: Hematoma (Acute vs. Organizing)
items: Within the [subcutaneous / intramuscular] layer at the site of prior trauma, there is a well-demarcated [echogenic (acute) / complex septated hypoechoic (subacute/organizing)] collection measuring [X.X] x [X.X] x [X.X] cm with no internal or peripheral Doppler vascularity, consistent with a hematoma.

subs.title: Postoperative Seroma
items: Deep to the surgical incision, there is a well-circumscribed, thin-walled anechoic fluid collection measuring [X.X] x [X.X] x [X.X] cm with posterior acoustic enhancement and absent internal Doppler flow, consistent with a postoperative seroma.

subs.title: Ganglion Cyst
items: Adjacent to the [dorsal wrist / volar radial wrist / ankle] joint capsule/tendon sheath, there is a well-defined, non-compressible [anechoic / multilocular] cystic lesion measuring [X.X] x [X.X] x [X.X] cm with posterior acoustic enhancement, a thin communicating neck extending toward the underlying [joint space / tendon sheath], and no internal Doppler flow, diagnostic of a ganglion cyst.

subs.title: Peripheral Nerve Sheath Tumor (Schwannoma / Neurofibroma)
items: Along the anatomical course of the [median / ulnar / radial / peroneal] nerve, there is a well-circumscribed, fusiform hypoechoic solid mass measuring [X.X] x [X.X] x [X.X] cm demonstrating direct continuity with the parent nerve fascicles at its proximal and distal poles ("rat-tail" sign), posterior acoustic enhancement, and mild internal Doppler vascularity, characteristic of a benign peripheral nerve sheath tumor.

subs.title: Retained Foreign Body (Wood / Glass / Metal)
items: Within the subcutaneous soft tissues approximately [X.X] mm deep to the skin surface, there is a linear hyperechoic focus measuring [X.X] mm in length casting [dense posterior acoustic shadowing (wood/thorn) / comet-tail reverberation artifact (glass/metal)], surrounded by a thin hypoechoic inflammatory halo with mild peripheral hyperemia, consistent with a retained foreign body.

subs.title: Reactive Benign Lymph Node
items: Oval, well-circumscribed lymph node measuring [X.X] x [X.X] cm with uniform thin hypoechoic cortex (less than 3 mm), preserved central echogenic fatty hilum, and normal hilar branching Doppler vascularity, consistent with a benign reactive lymph node.

subs.title: Suspicious / Pathologic Lymph Node
items: Enlarged, rounded lymph node measuring [X.X] x [X.X] cm demonstrating focal/diffuse cortical thickening, loss of the central echogenic fatty hilum, and aberrant peripheral capsular Doppler vascularity; tissue sampling / clinical correlation is recommended.
